questions.stem: A chemotherapy drug is classified as a vesicant. What is the key implication if the drug extravasates into surrounding tissue?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It can cause severe local tissue injury, including blistering, ulceration, or necrosis depending on the agent","B":"It causes only transient discomfort because vesicants cannot produce tissue necrosis after extravasation","C":"Its effects are exclusively systemic, so the infusion site does not require assessment during administration","D":"It is interchangeable with a nonvesicant irritant because both terms indicate the same degree of tissue injury"}}
questions.rationale: ONS extravasation guidance identifies extravasation of vesicants or irritants with vesicant properties as a potentially serious event that can cause pain, swelling, erythema and, in severe cases, tissue necrosis and ulceration. This supports option A and distinguishes vesicants from agents without comparable tissue-damaging potential.
questions.source_detail: Extravasation Management > Background; last reviewed September 18, 2025: severe extravasation can cause tissue necrosis and ulceration.

questions.stem: A client reports tremor and a rapid heartbeat after using inhaled albuterol. How should the nurse interpret these findings?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"They are recognized adverse effects of beta-adrenergic agonist therapy and should be assessed for severity and persistence","B":"They prove the medication is ineffective and require the client to double the next dose without further assessment","C":"They are unrelated to albuterol because inhaled beta agonists cannot produce systemic cardiovascular or neuromuscular effects","D":"They always indicate anaphylaxis and therefore establish a diagnosis of severe allergic reaction without other findings"}}
questions.rationale: Current albuterol labeling identifies tachycardia as a common adverse reaction and recognizes cardiovascular effects from beta-adrenergic stimulation; tremor is also a recognized beta-agonist effect. These findings require clinical assessment rather than automatic dose escalation or attribution to anaphylaxis.
questions.source_name: DailyMed — Albuterol Sulfate Inhalation Aerosol Prescribing Information
questions.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions 5.4 Cardiovascular Effects; Adverse Reactions 6.1 includes tachycardia; beta-adrenergic stimulation can also produce tremor.

questions.stem: A nurse manager uses a servant-leadership approach. Which behavior best reflects this leadership style?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Centralizing authority so staff members have little opportunity to develop autonomy or leadership capacity.","B":"Prioritizing the leader's status and recognition when those goals conflict with the growth of team members.","C":"Avoiding difficult decisions so responsibility for team outcomes rests entirely with frontline staff.","D":"Supporting the growth, development, and needs of team members while remaining accountable for leadership decisions and outcomes."}}
questions.rationale: The Open RN Nursing Management and Professional Concepts text describes servant leadership as focusing on the growth and well-being of team members, sharing in decision-making, and developing team members to their highest potential. This does not imply absent or avoidant leadership.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Management and Professional Concepts, 2nd ed.
questions.source_detail: Chapter 4 Leadership and Management, Table 4.2b Characteristics of Leadership Styles — Servant: focus on growth and well-being of team members, shared decision-making, development to highest potential.

questions.stem: A nurse educator explains the difference between a preceptor and a mentor. Which description best fits a preceptor?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A clinician assigned to provide structured, role-specific orientation, supervision, feedback, and skill development for a defined period.","B":"A person whose only function is long-term informal career advice without responsibility for clinical orientation or competency development.","C":"A role that is interchangeable with mentoring because preceptorship has no defined educational or clinical purpose.","D":"A manager who performs formal disciplinary evaluation but does not support transition into a clinical role or practice setting."}}
questions.rationale: Open RN describes orientation as competency-based and typically time-limited, with a novice nurse working with a preceptor. Preceptors are experienced nurses who serve as role models and resources, coach the new nurse into the role, evaluate performance, and provide feedback.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Health Alterations: Transition to Practice
questions.source_detail: Chapter 12.5 Transitioning to the PN Role > Orientation and Preceptors: orientation is competency-based; preceptors coach, evaluate performance, and provide feedback.

questions.stem: Which finding is classically associated with the chronic bronchitis phenotype of COPD rather than emphysema?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Chronic cough with sputum production; the traditional epidemiologic definition is cough and sputum for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years.","B":"Destruction of alveolar walls and enlargement of distal air spaces as the defining pathologic abnormality of the chronic bronchitis phenotype.","C":"Absence of cough and sputum because mucus hypersecretion is not associated with chronic bronchitis in patients with COPD.","D":"A disease pattern unrelated to tobacco exposure or other inhaled irritants, because airway inflammation is not involved in chronic bronchitis."}}
questions.rationale: GOLD retains chronic bronchitis as a clinically and epidemiologically useful term defined by cough and sputum production for at least 3 months in each of two consecutive years, while emphysema refers to destruction of gas-exchanging lung surfaces. The phenotypes can overlap and are not synonymous with COPD as a whole.
questions.source_name: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease — 2026 GOLD Report
questions.source_detail: 2026 GOLD Report / Digital GOLD Report, COPD definition discussion: chronic bronchitis is cough and sputum production for at least 3 months in each of two consecutive years; emphysema is destruction of gas-exchanging surfaces.
